description: this diagram represents the ripng (routing information protocol next generation) for ipv6. it shows how ripng operates on ipv6 networks, including the use of multiple ipv6 addresses on a single physical interface, split horizon, and administrative controls. the protocol operates on top of ipv6, utilizing its features like ip authentication header and ip encapsulating security payload for security. the diagram includes components such as routers, interfaces, link-local addresses, and routing tables.

elements.description: router managing the routing table and sending/receiving ripng packets.
physical or virtual interface connecting the router to the network.
multiple ipv6 addresses associated with a single physical interface.
a unique address used by routers on the local link, ensuring routing messages are delivered.
data structure containing routes and their attributes.
individual path from the source to the destination.
unique identifier for each route in the routing table.
routing control mechanism ensuring routes learned from a particular neighbor are not included in updates sent to that neighbor.
more robust version of split horizon, including routes learned from a neighbor with a metric of infinity.
filters and neighbor lists to restrict route exchange based on administrative or policy decisions.
